## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB16** Eleven sequencer and UI bugs fixed by ems-monomachine-firmware (Monomachine, OS 1.32B; open in stock; fixed by a custom firmware). Workaround: fixed in ems-monomachine-firmware (beta).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I38** Low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Cause: after the OS remaps CS0, nothing decodes the low window on hardware; the emulator maps flash at `0x0` and `0x10000000`. Fix: link and point through `0x10000000`; scan images for low pointers. Rules: A53.

## 9. All 53 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] Timing: 44.1 kHz, 32-sample blocks. DSP1 at 101.6064 MHz = 73,728 cycles per block. DSP2 at 98.784 MHz = 71,680 cycles per block. Its program never sets the PLL, so the boot stub's setting stays. The emulator clocks it at DSP1's rate and so overstates the budget. The two budgets cannot be pooled. `[hw]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#42cb8620` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:24](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L24) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
- [hw] The whole producer pass (16 renders plus dispatch, updates, interrupts and DMA waits) must fit in 71,680 cycles. A severe overrun on hardware first crackled, then lit every LED and left the engine silent. `[hw]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#bc6ffb77` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L30) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
- [hw] Per-track floor of ~3,290 cycles (measured on hardware): each track's 32-word block travels to DSP1 over ESSI0 at ~100 cycles a word, double-buffered. Track k's transfer runs during track k+1's render, so a track costs `max(render + ~40, ~3,290)`. Time saved below the floor is lost, not banked. Making a cheap machine cheaper gains nothing. `[hw]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#af43423f` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L31) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
- [hw] External-memory wait states (the emulator ignores them; measured on hardware): ~1 wait state in areas 0-2, ~5 in area 3 (`0x1C0000+`). A machine with many external accesses costs several thousand cycles more on hardware than in the emulator. `[hw]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#41446666` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L35) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
- [hw] Flash appears at both `0x0` and `0x10000000` in the emulator. On hardware, after the OS remaps CS0 nothing decodes the low window: images with low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Link and point through `0x10000000`, and scan images for low pointers. `[hw]` ([I38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i38-low-window-flash-pointers-boot-in-the-emulator-and-hang-on-the-unit)) — `machinedrum-monomachine#76388b6d` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:44](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L44) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
- [hw] `P:0x400-0x4FF` on DSP2 is not internal memory on hardware (the cache is on, so internal P ends at `0x3FF`). Early prototypes put code there. `[hw]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#8f6aa3ed` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L45) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
- [hw] ColdFire ISA: `movem.l d0-d1,-(sp)` is a 68000/68020 form ColdFire lacks. Emulators run a 68020 core, and the first trigger of every new machine froze the unit. Kitbasher allows only ISA_A for the MCF5206e (no MAC in added code) and decodes the final image from every entry point (rule A42). — `machinedrum-monomachine#71757ed4` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L53) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] Boot-time memory: Ordinary stores to flash relocation sites hung the unit at the boot screen; the emulator ignored them. Boot writes from `0x2bd000` up froze a MKII +Drive UW at the logo, while the same image without them booted. Use only hardware-proven RAM ranges. Boot code must not push registers before the OS has set up a stack. — `machinedrum-monomachine#7b0bf355` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:54](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L54) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] The host port to the DSPs holds about two words; the emulator buffers thousands. A sender whose poll timed out left DSP1's handler armed, so the next stock send was shifted by two words. A loader interleaving its writes with the OS's put a thousand words at a wrong address. Send exactly as stock does (interrupts masked) and own the port for the whole transfer. — `machinedrum-monomachine#d180082e` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:58](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L58) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] The per-step trigger loop is hot: a hook doing a table lookup and register save on every call froze the audio with 12-16 tracks triggering (CPU! lit). It was found only by a hardware bisect. Cache, then exit early. — `machinedrum-monomachine#09dbeb9f` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L62) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] Never remove stock DSP pacing. Replacing a 480-cycle DSP1 pad contributed to that freeze. Letting DSP2 skip ahead on silent tracks starved the ColdFire's stream and lost triggers. — `machinedrum-monomachine#7df074b9` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:63](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L63) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] No long `rep` on a DSP path: `rep #$600` (clearing 1,536 words) overran the CPU on the first P-I bass-drum trigger. Changing it to `rep #1` proved the cause; two stores per `do` pass fixed it. This is the same rule as on the Octatrack. — `machinedrum-monomachine#27e86e8c` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:64](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L64) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] The stock DSP1 watchdog: DSP1 counts blocks that DSP2 delivered late. On the third in a row it stops the output DMA and spins, silent until a power cycle. Half a percent over budget for three blocks is enough. — `machinedrum-monomachine#717ff659` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:65](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L65) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] DSP correctness traps: Nested `do` loops sharing an end address left state on the real hardware stack, and DSP2 hung. An inherited modulo register wrapped a 384-word clear into 32 words. DSP2 external RAM holds power-on garbage (the emulator reads zero), so init must clear everything it reads, and every block must write all 32 samples. — `machinedrum-monomachine#b8f43b7c` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L66) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
- [hw] Machine ids 124-127 fall inside the OS's "control machine" range tests. — `machinedrum-monomachine#f0a01cd5` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L70) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)

Declare minimum lengths. — `machinedrum-monomachine#78fe9953` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:71](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L71) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)

- [doc] CPU: ColdFire MCF5206E. It runs the OS (UI, sequencer, MIDI, kits, parameter conversion, flash, DSP control). Older notes say MCF5307; the board model and the MAME driver both identify an MCF5206E. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#5e78b344` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:16](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L16) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
- [doc] Links: ColdFire to each DSP over the HI08 host port. The DSP-side handler takes an address and a count and DMAs the words into Y memory; this is how parameters reach a voice. DSP2 to DSP1 over ESSI0 (one block per track); codec on ESSI1. MIDI on ColdFire UART1; front panel on UART2. The old idea that the ColdFire plays voices through a DSP SCI port is wrong. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#6e0aa523` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L19) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
- [doc] The reference assembler (mborgerson/dsp56300) accepts overlapping `ORG`s silently, so validate its output before packing: one contiguous segment, inside its bank, no warnings, entry points inside. A DO loop's end label goes on the instruction after the last loop instruction. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#f003c4a2` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:80](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L80) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
- [doc] The boot-ROM updater stages the whole image in RAM and checks it before the first erase, so an interrupted or corrupt transfer changes nothing. `[doc]` (code reading) — `machinedrum-monomachine#78950f33` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:84](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L84) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
- [doc] An exporter must include everything up to the last non-`0xFF` byte below `0x100000`. Custom code near `0xFE000-0xFFFFF` sits after the blob chain, and stopping at the last blob boots with pointers into erased flash. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#34ed77fe` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:86](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L86) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
- [doc] The trap: the OS rewrites the boot sector. On every boot, MainOS checks the magic word at flash `0x3FFE`. If it isn't `0x224B`, MainOS erases the boot sector and rewrites it from a copy embedded in MainOS. A modified OS that alters that check or that copy can destroy the updater on its first boot; after that only an external flash programmer helps. Same pattern as the A4 MK1, so rule A38 applies. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#23ac3c38` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:87](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L87) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
- [doc] Recovery otherwise: enter the boot ROM's upgrade mode and send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI (the unit has no USB). Rule A36. `[doc]` — `machinedrum-monomachine#a199f222` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:88](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L88) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
- [doc] Monomodule runs the Monomachine's own sound engine in an emulated DSP56300 and matches the hardware sample for sample. So the sound engine is DSP56300 code taken from the OS file (OS 1.32B, `Elektron_SFX6-60_OS1.32B.syx`). `[doc]` {monomodule} — `machinedrum-monomachine#30902ba3` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:91](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L91) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
- [doc] Custom OS saved-data hazard: em's firmware reclaims song slots for extended data (MnM: slots 13-24; MD: 13-32). Songs left in those slots are corrupted on boot, so back them up first. The same can happen with any mod that changes saved-data layouts (compare section E of AGENT-RULES). `[doc]` {ems-fw} — `machinedrum-monomachine#9b28e640` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:101](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L101) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
- [doc] em's firmware carries features from jmamma's MDX (new machines, tunings, LFO shapes, MIDI fixes) with credit. `[doc]` {ems-fw} — `machinedrum-monomachine#76db16b6` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:102](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L102) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
- [doc] Screen dump (ems-monomachine-firmware 26B09): the request `F0 00 20 3C 03 00 64 F7` returns 16 SysEx chunks of 7-bit-packed data, 64 bytes each once decoded: the native LCD bitmap, 128x64, 1 bit, column-major, bottom to top, MSB first. Whether stock 1.32B answers it is not stated. The firmware is now compressed, so boot is slower. `[doc]` {ems-mnm-changelog} — `machinedrum-monomachine#955184aa` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:104](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L104) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)

- [untagged] joelanders/gearmulator-md-mm source (`source/elektron/md/mdLib`: memory map, types, board scheduler comments). Key {gearmulator-md-mm}. Projects: [../../catalog/machinedrum.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/catalog/machinedrum.md), [../../catalog/monomachine.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/catalog/monomachine.md). The short version: an early-2000s three-chip design (an old ColdFire plus two Motorola DSP56303s). It is nothing like the DT2/DN2: no SHARC, no FreeRTOS budget model, and no USB. Its flash updater lives in a boot sector that the OS itself can rewrite. — `machinedrum-monomachine#4b4a480c` [hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/machinedrum-monomachine.md#L9) · Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60)

- [untagged] `move #16,a` loads a fraction (`a1 = $100000`), not 16. Write integers into data-ALU registers in the long form `#>16`.
